# Upload-sized archive parts

Choose the format from the receiver's actual capabilities. Raw `.zip.part01` fragments
are not standalone ZIPs: all parts must be rejoined before extraction. If a review tool
needs independently readable uploads and cannot reassemble, partition the source files
into separate valid archives instead. Preserve the original archive in either case.

## Decide the count and freeze the source

- Confirm either a fixed count N or a maximum per-file byte count B (or both).
  MB is 1,000,000 bytes; MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. Resolve ambiguous limits explicitly.
- For source size S and a cap B, use N = ceil(S/B), equivalently (S+B-1)//B.
  For a fixed N, respect that count; check ceil(S/N) <= B when a cap also applies.
  If the constraints conflict, resolve them before splitting. Balanced parts differ
  by at most one byte when S is not divisible by N; never silently pad the archive.
  An empty source or N > S needs an explicit decision about empty parts.
- Freeze the completed archive: record its exact byte count and SHA256, and ensure
  no producer is still writing it. Preserve it until delivery verification completes.
  Use the project's housing/back-up rules for large files and retained copies.

GNU commands below are an example for 17 parts, not a default count, size or destination.
Replace quoted paths and numeric arguments with the values chosen for this request.
On macOS use GNU coreutils `gstat`, `gsplit`, `gsha256sum` and `gmv` where applicable, or create on Linux.
Prefer an existing archive publisher or transfer tool over writing a new wrapper.

```sh
stat --format=%s -- "/store/review.zip"
sha256sum -- "/store/review.zip"
mkdir -m 700 -- "/delivery/.review-parts-staging"
split --number=17 --numeric-suffixes=1 --suffix-length=2 -- "/store/review.zip" "/delivery/.review-parts-staging/review.zip.part"
```

Create a new private, empty staging folder outside the source clone; `mkdir` must fail
if it already exists. For a byte cap, calculate N first, then pass that N to `--number`:
for S=103 bytes and B=10 bytes use `--number=11` (four 10-byte, seven 9-byte parts).
Do not substitute `--bytes=B` when balanced sizes are requested. Numeric suffixes start
at 1; choose width at least the decimal digit count of N (two digits for 01 through 99).
The fixed-width suffix must be consistent across the whole set.

## Verify and package before publishing

Work inside the staging directory. With the example's two-digit suffixes:

```sh
cd "/delivery/.review-parts-staging"
stat --format='%n %s' -- review.zip.part[0-9][0-9]
sha256sum -- review.zip.part[0-9][0-9] > SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
cat -- review.zip.part[0-9][0-9] | sha256sum
cat -- review.zip.part[0-9][0-9] | wc -c
```

Check the exact count N, uninterrupted suffixes 01..17, expected floor(S/N) or
ceil(S/N) sizes, total S and every size <= B if capped. Compare the streamed joined
SHA256 to the frozen original, not just to a newly generated part manifest. Stop on
any mismatch. Recheck the source's size and hash if it could have changed.

Include `SHA256SUMS` (relative part filenames) and `REASSEMBLE.txt`. The latter records
the original filename, exact byte count and SHA256, N, suffix width, ordered part list,
and complete receiver commands. It must say to download every part into one folder,
verify parts, rejoin in numeric order, verify original size/hash, then extract.
For larger sets, update the width and recipes; use the manifest's explicit order
instead of a broad wildcard that might include other files or misorder suffixes.

POSIX receiver example for exactly 17 two-digit parts, from their directory:

```sh
sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
cat review.zip.part0[1-9] review.zip.part1[0-7] > review.zip
wc -c < review.zip
sha256sum review.zip
```

On macOS, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS` and `shasum -a 256 review.zip` work.
Windows `cmd.exe` example (keep the copy command on one line):

```bat
copy /b review.zip.part01+review.zip.part02+review.zip.part03+review.zip.part04+review.zip.part05+review.zip.part06+review.zip.part07+review.zip.part08+review.zip.part09+review.zip.part10+review.zip.part11+review.zip.part12+review.zip.part13+review.zip.part14+review.zip.part15+review.zip.part16+review.zip.part17 review.zip
certutil -hashfile review.zip SHA256
```

Windows users can check each part with `certutil -hashfile PART SHA256` against
`SHA256SUMS`, and the joined size with PowerShell `(Get-Item 'review.zip').Length`.
Do not use text-mode concatenation or overwrite an existing reconstructed archive.

## Deliver the verified set

Publish the complete verified folder with an existing atomic publisher, or a rename
on the same filesystem to a fresh final name. With GNU coreutils, `mv -T -n --
STAGING FINAL` avoids replacing an existing destination; check that the staging path
is gone and the intended final folder exists (a skipped move can return success).
For another filesystem, copy to private staging on that filesystem, verify there,
then rename locally. Do not merge into or overwrite someone else's files.

Copy only to destinations authorized for this request; a past Boiler Downloads path
is an example, not continuing permission. Ensure the intended user can read and owns
the delivery as required. At each delivered copy verify the part manifest and streamed
joined SHA256/byte count again; streaming avoids another archive-sized temporary copy.
Report the final path, N, byte bounds, original hash and reassembly instructions.
